answer: Pearl Island Forging Each agent identity is anchored to a unique physical sensor node deployed on a monitored geographic island. The node continuously streams timestamped environmental data—light, sound, temperature—to a public ledger. To forge a new identity, an attacker must replicate both the sensor hardware and its exact environmental context at a remote location. This requires matching real-time conditions across multiple dimensions, which is physically impossible to sustain without occupying the actual island.
